note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §7, §9, §13.7, Stage 92; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 11) on data/benches/copper_cycle.json: the copper cycle from copper nitrate, four compounds and back to the metal, and the percent recovery.
title: Experiment: the copper cycle

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: The copper goes through four compounds and back to the metal. What share of the 0.500 g of copper do you expect to get back, in per cent?

steps.title: Base in excess
steps.text: Pick up the sodium hydroxide, right-click the beaker, type 10 and click "pour"; right-click the beaker and stir it.
steps.why: Cu2+ + 2 OH- -> Cu(OH)2, pale blue. 10 mL of 2 M base is about 20 mmol of hydroxide, for 15.7 mmol needed: the rest stays, and helps the next step.

steps.title: Heat it
steps.text: Pick up the burner and click the beaker, so it stands under it; right-click the burner and open its valve about two thirds.

steps.title: It turns black
steps.text: Watch the blue turn black as it nears 90 C: copper oxide.
steps.why: Copper oxide is a little more stable than the hydroxide. In the hot base the hydroxide dissolves as Cu(OH)4 2-, and black copper oxide grows from it: Cu(OH)2 -> CuO + H2O. In water, or cold, it would take months.

steps.title: Sulfuric acid
steps.text: Pour 11 mL of the sulfuric acid into the beaker, still stirred, and wait for the black to dissolve.
steps.why: CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O, blue again. 16.5 mmol of acid: it neutralises the leftover base, dissolves the oxide, and a little is left over.

steps.title: Magnesium
steps.text: Pick up the dish of magnesium, right-click the beaker and click "tip in". It fizzes, and red-brown copper comes out as the blue fades.
steps.why: Mg + Cu2+ -> Mg2+ + Cu: magnesium is more reactive than copper. The leftover acid takes some of it as hydrogen, so it goes in excess.

steps.title: The leftover magnesium
steps.text: Pour 10 mL of the hydrochloric acid in and wait for the fizzing to stop: the magnesium left over dissolves, the copper does not.
steps.why: Mg + 2 HCl -> MgCl2 + H2; copper is less reactive than hydrogen.

steps.title: The funnel on the flask
steps.text: Pick up the funnel and click the flask: it stands in its neck.

steps.title: Pour it through
steps.text: Pick up the beaker, right-click the funnel, type 80 and click "pour".

steps.title: The rest of the copper
steps.text: Pick up the beaker again, right-click the funnel and click "tip in": the copper left in it.

steps.title: Until it has drained
steps.text: Wait for the funnel to drain.

steps.title: The dish on the balance
steps.text: Pick up the dish and click the balance; right-click the balance and tare it.

checks.text: the dish on the balance, tared

steps.title: The copper into the dish
steps.text: Pick up the funnel, right-click the dish and click "tip in": the copper scraped off the paper.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: The copper came off the paper warm, and warms the air in the dish: wait until the dish is back at the room's temperature.
steps.why: Warm air in and over the dish is lighter than the room's: it buoys the load, and the balance reads low (here by some 10 mg). Never weigh anything warm.

steps.title: Its mass
steps.text: Right-click the balance and write down what it reads.

report.label: the copper recovered
report.why: What the balance reads, the dish tared: the copper scraped off the paper.

report.label: the percent recovery
report.why: 100 x the copper recovered / 0.500 g. What is lost: on the paper, and copper never put out of the solution.
